9.9.1. qnav.quantum.base

9.9.1.1. base.py

summary:

Provides basic concept quantum sensors and fusion methods. These serve as base models that more advanced and realistic implementations can extend from.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation of class.

class qnav.quantum.base.ConceptQuantumImu(full_frequency: float, imu_frequency: float, accelerometer_errors: ~qnav.measurement.error_properties.ErrorProperties, gyroscope_errors: ~qnav.measurement.error_properties.ErrorProperties, sensor_axis: ~qnav.measurement.platform.SensorAxis = <qnav.measurement.platform.SensorAxis object>, duty_cycle: float = 0.5, start_time: float = 0.0, rand_seed: int = None)[source]

Concept Quantum IMU featuring use of quantum accelerometer and gyroscope. While not realistic in implementation, this base class produces measurements mimicking a quantum accelerometer and gyroscope, requiring multiple samples of the ground truth.

take_measurement(est_time: float, ground_truth: GroundTruth)[source]

Samples from the ground truth to collect data to produce measurements. Using the ground truth, captures the current acceleration and angles rates at the time. A series of these are required to produce a measurement before fusion.

Parameters:

  • est_time (float) – The estimated time the measurement of the sensor is expected to be captured at (in seconds).

  • ground_truth (GroundTruth) – The corresponding ground truth data.

update(time_sec: float = None)[source]

Called on demand to update the sensor’s state. Typically called after measurements have been taken. When called this increases the next measurement time and propagates internal states, to the time difference.

Parameters:

time_sec (float) – The current simulation time in seconds.

reset()[source]

Resets the sensor, clearing all previous measurements. Normally used directly after fusion.

property last_measurement: tuple[ndarray, ndarray]

Returns the last acceleration and angle rate measurements captured by the quantum sensor, respectively.

Returns:

The last measurements of the sensor.

Return type:

tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

class qnav.quantum.base.ConceptQuantumFusion(qs_imu: ConceptQuantumImu, shared_accelerometer: Accelerometer, shared_gyroscope: Gyroscope, est_qs_imu_axis: SensorAxis = None, est_acc_axis: SensorAxis = None, est_gyro_axis: SensorAxis = None)[source]

A basic version of quantum fusion, namely used as a base class. This is the simplest implementation of position correction fusion for quantum IMU. Many of its methods can be extended and swapped out for more advanced implementations.

perform_fusion(estimated_state: EstimatedState) → None[source]

Collects measurements and applies position fixing. Each cycle collects measurements from the typical IMU sensors and quantum sensor. After a set number of calls, this uses the single quantum measurement to calculate an approximate bias correction for the IMU. If successful, the position fixing is applied.

Parameters:

estimated_state (EstimatedState) – The current estimated state to update.

reset()[source]

Resets the state of the fusion, clearing internal temporary states. When call the fusion will return to expecting the first measurement, then continuing from there.
